prompt: A car travels at $60$ miles per hour. There are $5{,}280$ feet in a mile and $3{,}600$ seconds in an hour. What is the car's speed, in feet per second?
hint: Two units have to change: miles into feet and hours into seconds. Write each conversion as a fraction so unwanted units cancel.

hints.text: Two units have to change: miles into feet and hours into seconds. Write each conversion as a fraction so unwanted units cancel.
Multiply $60$ by $5280$ to change miles to feet, and divide by $3600$ to change hours to seconds: $\dfrac{60 \times 5280}{3600}$.
The result is $\dfrac{316800}{3600} = 88$, so the speed is $88$ feet per second.

learningObjective: Chain unit conversions using dimensional analysis.
explanation: Write each conversion as a fraction placed so that the unit you want to remove cancels.
Multiplying $60$ miles per hour by $5280$ feet per mile cancels miles. Dividing by $3600$ seconds per hour cancels hours.
Carrying out the arithmetic gives $\dfrac{60 \times 5280}{3600} = \dfrac{316800}{3600} = 88$, with feet per second as the unit left over.
The speed of the car is $88$ feet per second.

alternativeExplanations.title: Units are a free error check
steps: If the units left standing are not the ones the question asked for, you have flipped a factor.
That check catches the mistake *before* you do any arithmetic, which is when it is cheapest to fix.
Worth memorizing: $60$ mph is exactly $88$ ft/s. It shows up often enough to recognize.
